title: Vaccination trials on hold: malicious and low credibility content on Twitter during the AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine development
screen_reason: Observational Twitter study of COVID-19 vaccine discussion (1-15 September 2020) that reports the share of shared links, and the share of messages carrying such links, coming from low-credibility web domains as rated by Media Bias/Fact Check and The Factual: '14,215 (2%) URLs from 377 low credibility information sources that are shared in 42,271 (2.7%) messages posted before the halt of trials'. Per the governing denominator rule, a share of shared links that are unreliable is SHARING (content_share), not CONTENT.

estimates.country: Not stated (global Twitter stream, keyword-collected; content in multiple languages)
estimates.date: 1-15 September 2020, split at the 9 September trial halt into 'before' (Sept 1-8) and 'after' (Sept 9-15)
estimates.measure_type: % of COVID-19 vaccine tweets that shared a URL from a low-credibility web domain
estimates.value_raw: 42,271 (2.7%) messages before the halt; 36,906 (2.7%) messages after the halt
estimates.denominator: Twitter messages posted in the period in the keyword collection on COVID-19 vaccines (the full collection comprises 3,212,586 messages without URLs, by 1,788,788 users, and 3,958,864 messages containing at least one URL, by 1,267,873 users, citing 3,247,946 distinct URLs from 167,186 distinct web domains); the exact denominator behind the 2.7% is not printed
estimates.definition: A message counted if it cited a URL whose parent web domain was rated by Media Bias/Fact Check or The Factual as a questionable source, conspiracy-pseudoscience, or (very) low credibility
estimates.misinfo_def: “We considered as low credibility those web domains that were in at least one of the following categories: questionable sources, conspiracy-pseudoscience, or (very)low credibility rating.”
estimates.n: Not printed for this percentage; the tweet corpus for 1-15 September 2020 (3,958,864 messages contained at least one URL)
estimates.source_quote: We identified 14,215 (2%) URLs from 377 low credibility information sources that are shared in 42,271 (2.7%) messages posted before the halt of trials, and 12,768 URLs from 363 low credibility sources shared in 36,906 (2.7%) messages posted after the halt of trials.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two published domain-credibility lists: Media Bias/Fact Check (MBFC 2020) and The Factual (2020); a domain counted as low credibility if listed in at least one of 'questionable sources', 'conspiracy-pseudoscience', or '(very) low credibility'. No inter-rater reliability applies (list lookup); no validation of list coverage reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: We collected tweets using the Twitter API from 1st of September 2020 to 15th of September 2020. The original keywords used to collect this dataset are AstraZeneca, "Astra Zeneca", AZD1222, COVID, vaccine, immunity, "herd immunity", Barrington, and "focused protection". ... We used the vaccine-related keywords in the regex condition: pfizer OR astrazeneca OR moderna OR (sputnik AND vaccine) to select tweets relevant to our study.
estimates.notes: Time series collapsed to one point per the instructions: the two periods (before / after the 9 September halt) give the SAME message-level percentage, 2.7%, so a single row carries both verbatim. Confidence is medium only because the raw denominator behind the 2.7% is never printed - the numerators (42,271 and 36,906) and the percentages are both verbatim, but the base is implicit. Note this is a source-level (domain-list) measure, so breadth is blank per the schema rule. QUOTE NOTE: the extracted .txt hyphenates 'mes-/sages' across a line break, so this sentence is not a contiguous string in the .txt; it is otherwise exact, and quote_verbatim is set to false.

estimates.value_raw: 14,215 (2%) URLs from 377 low credibility information sources
estimates.denominator: Distinct URLs cited in the tweets collected before the halt (the whole 1-15 September collection cites 3,247,946 distinct URLs from 167,186 distinct web domains); the exact denominator behind the 2% is not printed
estimates.definition: A URL counted if its parent web domain was rated by Media Bias/Fact Check or The Factual as a questionable source, conspiracy-pseudoscience, or (very) low credibility
estimates.misinfo_def: “We considered as low credibility those web domains that were in at least one of the following categories: questionable sources, conspiracy-pseudoscience, or (very)low credibility rating.”
estimates.n: Not printed; distinct URLs cited in the Sept 1-8 tweets (whole collection: 3,247,946 distinct URLs)
estimates.source_quote: We identified 14,215 (2%) URLs from 377 low credibility information sources
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Media Bias/Fact Check and The Factual domain lists; URLs represented by their parent domain after shortener expansion and parameter stripping.
estimates.moderator_quote: We grouped the web domains according to the classification made by two sources (i.e., Media Bias/Fact Check (MBFC 2020) and the Factual (Factual 2020).
estimates.notes: Same construct and ground truth as the message-level row but a different unit of count (distinct URLs rather than messages), hence definition_variant=true. The corresponding after-halt URL percentage is NOT reported (only the count, 12,768), so no second period row is possible for this unit. QUOTE NOTE: trimmed to the span that is contiguous in the extracted .txt (the sentence continues 'that are shared in 42,271 (2.7%) messages posted before the halt of trials', but 'messages' is hyphenated across a line break).

missed_or_uncertain: 1) MALICIOUS URLs: the paper's second content stream (VirusTotal-flagged phishing/malware URLs) never reports a share of URLs that are malicious - only properties OF the malicious set (35.9% / 25.9% use shorteners, 80.04% hosted on CDNs, 33.5% on public cloud, 30.80% / 40.66% of their domains ranked below 100K on Alexa). Those denominators are the malicious set itself, not the corpus, so they are within-set descriptors and not prevalence; they are also a security rather than a veracity construct. No row. 2) COORDINATION network shares - '56 [edges] are to low credibility sources, which is 2% of the total edges in the original coordinated network' (before), '58 ... which also represents 2%' (after), and '188 ... which is 6%' / '130 ... 4.7%' for malicious edges - are shares of network EDGES inside a filtered coordinated-sharing subnetwork, not a share of items, users or exposure in the corpus, and are not a CONCENTRATION statement (no top-X% group with a matching share of activity), so R1 cannot be met. 3) The conclusion's '36%' of low-credibility and malicious URLs using shorteners vs '<1%' of non-malicious contradicts the body figures (35.9% vs 20.2%) - an internal inconsistency worth flagging but not extractable. 4) Table 3 and Table 6 give per-domain tweet/user/URL counts with no denominators. 5) Growth figures (363.7% increase in AstraZeneca tweets, 149.1% Pfizer, -50.2% SputnikV, -57.5% Moderna) are change rates, not shares. 6) Topic-model tweet counts (Tables 1-2) have no misinformation numerator.

rob.design: Keyword-collected Twitter API census, 1-15 September 2020 (AstraZeneca / COVID / vaccine terms, then filtered to pfizer OR astrazeneca OR moderna OR sputnik+vaccine); 3,958,864 URL-bearing messages by 1,267,873 users citing 3,247,946 distinct URLs from 167,186 domains, plus 3,212,586 messages without URLs by 1,788,788 users. No sampling of users, no response rate (trace data). Credibility coded automatically by domain lookup against Media Bias/Fact Check and The Factual; maliciousness by VirusTotal (>70 AV engines, flagged if >=1 engine positive, a very permissive threshold). Only the top two malicious URL clusters were manually verified. No inter-coder reliability. Denominators for the headline percentages are not printed; authors note they could not filter out organic simultaneous sharing (share-button artefacts) in the coordination analysis.
